summary: FINAL GATING CLAIM — tools/governor/footer.mjs ONLY, the renderer, parser and degradation ladder of the governor footer. FOURTH REVIEW OF THIS SCOPE; the three prior ones each returned request_changes and EACH WAS RIGHT. Their four findings are fixed and are described below so you can attack the repairs rather than rediscover the defects. CONTEXT. BUILD-018 built a session governor that enforced 0 of its 4 intended rules and is being torn down surgically rather than reverted. footer.mjs SURVIVES. It is the ONLY governor output that reaches the operator on the claude.ai web and Android clients, where the terminal statusLine never runs — that is why it exists, and why its honesty matters more than its coverage. WHAT THIS DIFF DOES. (1) footer.mjs drops its programme-state dependency, one of the two surgical decouplings in the teardown. (2) `next:` becomes a CALLER-SUPPLIED input defaulting to UNSET; nextModelFor and the programme-shaped UNSET_REASON members are deleted, because nothing can emit them once their producer is gone. It carries MODEL and EFFORT together, as in 'Opus/high', with both vocabularies frozen as literals that the renderer AND the anchored FOOTER_RE derive from, so the two cannot drift. (3) HANDBACK_CODES is byte-identical to a989e68 — the frozen mirror of the constitution's seven interruption codes, so an edit there is a breaking change to a governing document rather than a code edit. (4) The context indicator is re-sourced from the session transcript so a reading reaches the operator on clients where statusLine never runs. THE GOVERNING RULE FOR THE INDICATOR, ruled by the operator: accept a TRUE ABSOLUTE COUNT on web and mobile; never use a static declared window; never infer a denominator from another session; render a PERCENTAGE ONLY when the current session supplies an authoritative window size. A wrong percentage is strictly worse than no percentage — a prior defect rendered a live session at 46% of a borrowed window when its true figure was 9%. THE FOUR PRIOR FINDINGS AND THEIR REPAIRS, so you can test my account rather than accept it. (F1) render/parse lost a permitted usedTokens value when a percent was present with no windowTokens; the bare-percent shape has nowhere to put a numerator, so it was dropped and the round-trip identity was false for that shape. Fixed by REFUSING that combination outright. (F2) the token codec failed for values reaching exponent notation, which the decimal-only parser rejects. I initially rebutted this by probing decade values to 1e22 and reported the mechanism 'disproven'; THAT REBUTTAL WAS WRONG AND IS FORMALLY WITHDRAWN — the accepted domain also contained a LOSSY class far below any exponent threshold, where 100000000000001200 rendered as '100000000000001.2k' and parsed back as 100000000000001180 with ok:true. Fixed by bounding the codec at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and checking toRenderableTokens' RESULT rather than its argument, because rounding can cross the bound upward. (F3) the percentage was DIVIDED FROM DISPLAY-ROUNDED tokens. I adjudicated this negligible — real windows are grain-aligned and the error is ~0.025%, below the integer percent rendered — AND I WAS WRONG, because the value feeds a THRESHOLD and a step function turns an arbitrarily small error into a maximal one at a boundary. An exhaustive sweep moved 5,096 rendered lines and 50 CLEAR NOW instructions; at used=149,950 of 200,000 the true figure is 74.975% but the numerator rounded to exactly 75.000%, crossing RED and telling the operator to discard a healthy session — while the DISPLAYED percentage read 75% either way and hid it completely. Fixed by dividing the authoritative raw values, with the rendered token fields still grain-aligned. (F4) INV-1 WAS BREACHED: the out-of-range guard ran AFTER Math.round, and Math.round(-0.4) is -0 while -0 < 0 is false, so used_percentage -0.4 rendered 'ctx 0% GREEN'. The breach band is [-0.5, 0) low and (100, 100.5) high, asymmetric because Math.round is round-half-up; the high side rendered RED, which is a graded state from an unrepresentable input but NOT a false GREEN. Fixed by judging the raw value before rounding. A fifth defect surfaced with it: percent -0 rendered '0%' and parsed back as +0, so the round-trip identity was false for a value the renderer accepts — and the suite was STRUCTURALLY BLIND to it because assert.deepEqual(-0, 0) passes. Fixed by normalising in the producer, asserted with Object.is. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: tools/governor/continuity.mjs and continuity-derive.mjs have NO TESTS AT ALL — zero coverage, not merely unproven wiring; worktree-guard.mjs survives as a file but is INERT, returning defer for every guarded tool once no active programme-state exists, reported deliberately and NOT repaired because building a replacement guard is the regrowth this reset exists to cut; renderFooter still accepts percent:-0 from a DIRECT caller, unreachable through the producer but open to a caller hand-building fields. CI DOES run this suite on windows-latest — 214 executed and passing at an earlier head, since risen — but has not run against this exact head. All other evidence is builder self-test plus my own independent re-run of every number. It is NOT independent review, which is what you are being asked for.
brief_excerpt:
Judge this diff against these acceptance criteria and ONLY these. C4 and D1-D6 were written BEFORE the diff existed.

SCOPE. This packet contains tools/governor/footer.mjs ONLY, and the packet's own diff_range now states that scope explicitly rather than leaving it to this prose. Three notes so a scope artefact is never mistaken for a defect. (1) Rows about any other file are OUT OF SCOPE — mark them not_applicable, never blocked, and do not let the absence of other files reduce confidence in the rows below. (2) The tests for this module live in tools/governor/footer.test.mjs, a SEPARATE file whose diff exceeds the review cap and CANNOT be staged untruncated — so do not report tests as missing from this packet, and do not infer from their absence that they do not exist. That limit is disclosed, not implied. (3) tools/governor/sampler.mjs, which supplies the sample, was reviewed under its own claim and approved twice; denominator ESTABLISHMENT is its responsibility, not this file's.

HAND-CARRIED PRIOR FINDINGS — DISCLOSED. There is no automated route by which prior review findings reach you; this tool takes only a claim file I author. The four findings summarised above were TRANSCRIBED BY ME BY HAND. Treat my account of what was fixed as an assertion to TEST, not a fact to accept.

C4. footer.mjs no longer imports programme-state.mjs.
D1. `next:` is caller-supplied, defaults to UNSET; nextModelFor and the programme-shaped UNSET_REASON members are deleted, not merely unused.
D2. The grammar is MODEL '/' EFFORT (e.g. Opus/high), UNSET still bare. BOTH vocabularies must be frozen literals that the renderer and FOOTER_RE derive from, so a change in one cannot drift from the other. Effort vocabulary is low|medium|high|xhigh|max.
D3. parseFooter(renderFooter(x)) round-trip identity holds across the ACCEPTED domain. Note this row was broken by TWO prior findings — verify the identity now holds for every representable CTX shape, that unrepresentable shapes are refused loudly rather than rendered lossily, and that it holds under Object.is and not merely loose equality, since loose equality is what hid the -0 case.
D4. HANDBACK_CODES is UNCHANGED — seven members, exact spelling. The constitution names it as the frozen mirror of the seven interruption codes, so any edit is a breaking change rather than an edit. HIGHEST SEVERITY ROW: check the member names character by character.
D6. A percentage must never be FABRICATED — never computed from a denominator that was guessed, borrowed from another session, or otherwise not established. It is NOT that a percentage requires token counts. Two honest sources, both acceptable: (i) a percentage the runtime REPORTED DIRECTLY in used_percentage, the statusLine path, which involves no denominator at all; or (ii) one DIVIDED from a real numerator by an authoritative denominator, the transcript path. When neither is available, render a true absolute token count if the numerator is known and leave the state ungraded.
D8. The token codec must be FAITHFUL across the whole domain isRenderableTokens accepts: formatTokens then parseTokens must return the original value exactly, with no lossy pair anywhere. Do NOT defer to any earlier rebuttal of this row, INCLUDING MINE — I argued the exponent mechanism was disproven by probing decades to 1e22 and that argument was wrong and is withdrawn. The claimed boundary is Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Attack it directly and give a CONCRETE value if you assert a break, paying particular attention to values near the bound, since rounding onto the display grain can move a value ACROSS it.

Z1. INV-1, the invariant this module exists for: BLIND must never render as GREEN. Verify no path through the ladder reaches a graded state from unreadable, stale, foreign, absent or UNREPRESENTABLE telemetry. This row was BREACHED by a prior finding and is the one that matters most — attack the repair rather than confirming it. Consider specifically any value that is out of the grammar's range but rounds into it, and any signed-zero or near-boundary case.
Z2. THE DEGRADATION LADDER must never throw. NOTE THE DISTINCTION AND TEST IT: renderFooter deliberately DOES throw on field combinations it cannot represent, on the reasoning that those indicate a caller bug and that silently dropping a field is worse than refusing it. Those two positions are compatible ONLY if no input the ladder can produce ever reaches a throwing combination. Verify that specifically — if any telemetry, however corrupt, can drive the producer into a combination renderFooter rejects, the ladder throws in exactly the situation it exists to survive.
Z3. Session-mismatch must outrank staleness, so a sample that is both stale AND from another session reports the mismatch.

ADVERSARIAL ROWS — answer even if every row above passes.
W1. Find any input for which the ladder renders a GRADED state the telemetry does not support. Name it concretely.
W2. Can renderFooter emit a line parseFooter cannot parse, or that parses to different values? Consider boundary numbers, rounding onto the display grain, signed zero, and the approximate marker.
W3. Any path where a real percentage is rendered from a denominator the sample did not authoritatively carry?
W4. The grammar is anchored by a regex. Can any permitted field value break the separator grammar or make the line ambiguous?
W5. Two repairs narrowed accepted domains. Does either narrow anything a REAL caller legitimately needs — does any honest telemetry value now get refused or degraded that previously rendered correctly? A repair that fixes a defect by discarding a real use case is a different defect.
W6. The percentage is now divided from raw values while the displayed token pair remains grain-rounded, so the two are no longer guaranteed to agree by construction. Is there any realistic input where that divergence misleads a reader?

OUT OF SCOPE — do not report as defects: which modules were kept or deleted (an operator decision); prose, naming or comment-style preference; the deliberate choice that a token count WITHOUT a denominator yields BLIND rather than a grade, which is ruled behaviour because a count cannot be classified without a window; the absence of malicious-handler hardening, since this estate's bar is correctness, accidental leak, availability and audit for a first-party personal system, not a hostile-input service; and the zero coverage of continuity.mjs plus the inert worktree-guard.mjs, both disclosed above and already recorded.
